sections.content:
See other comments, I will not repeat here.
The content is diverse and interesting, I enrolled this course for my personal interest even though I will not study further on communication protocals.
One of the best thing in this course is that it uses gradescope to grade all the things (hw, project, mt, finals), you don't need to do paper checking at their offices. Hope other courses in UST can follow this strategy.
There is also an ed discussion, which is convenient for us to ask once we have questions. You can also see other's questions, they may inspire you sometimes.
sections.teaching:
Professor Meng's teaching is quite good, his English accent is quite comfortable. Once you have question, you can directly ask and he will help you solve the problem immediately. If this happens during lectures, you will ask get candy! Professor Meng uses candy to boost students participate his class.
Before exams, he will release past paper and teach some problems. For the rest of questions, he will not release answers so that you should go to his office to ask. He also has an emergency office hour before final exam, please go there no matter you have questions or not. Since other students' questions are also worth to go revision.
sections.grading:
Grading policy:
Homework: 32% (8% each)
Projects: 20% (4 checkpoints (CP), 5% each)
Midterm: 20%
Final: 30%
You are given 4 ''slip days'' for free, so that you can hand on homework or project late when you are also busy on other subjects' due at the same time.
Professor Meng has a grade promise:
If your grade is >= 90%, you will get at least an A-
If your grade is >= 80%, you will get at least a B-
If your grade is >= 70%, you will get at least a C-
If your grade is >= 60%, you will get at least a D
Figures for midterm and final before paper checking:
Midterm:
Top 1,2,3: 90, 82.5, 81
10%: 69
25%: 60.5
50%: 46.5
Mean: 46
Final:
Top 1,2,3: 93.0, 92.5, 92.5
25%: 81.0
Median: 72.5
My score as reference:
I am slightly above UQ in midterm and just UQ in final, totally I have about 88/102 and get an A. The grading is quite good, I thought I will get A-, many thanks to professor. Perhaps the midterm and projects are very difficult.
For the assignment and exams, the grading is just normal. But for project, in the first three CPs, you will get full marks once you satisfy all the requirements. However in CP4, the grading becomes interesting. It lets us to design our own algorithm, the mark for it is basic mark+1st (shorest) execution time/your excution time * 10
sections.workload:
The homework is normal, not too much workload, the same as first two CPs. However, for CP3 and CP4, you do need much more time to understand. The skeleton code they gave has already been very long, I strongly recommend you to use AI tools to help you go through the C++ code and know where to add code. Especially for CP4, it is quite annoying, you can get 20 marks for the code if you directly send the code from CP3, for the rest of 20 marks. You have to come up with an algorithm that can cost you much less execution time. That is quite annoying even if you use ai to help you. Once you done it, you will become an expert in C++, hahaha.
For exams, your are allowed to take 2 A4 papers on both sides as cheat sheet, remember to leave some time to do it. I can share my method, I didn't make the cheat sheet directly, instead, I take some notes when I first study those materials and I just compact those notes into 4 pages and directly print out. Also, remember to take some time to get familiar with your cheat sheet, it is awful when you face a concept that you remember you have written it down to the cheat sheet but you cannot find it.

sections.content:
Mainly About different layers of internet
Application layer
Transport layer
Network layer
Data Link layer
Physical layer
Some other topics such as CDN, very basic security stuff will be covered at the end of the course.
The prerequisite for this course is COMP1021, however, make sure you know C++ while taking this course, because the project is using C++, even if you take COMP2011, it may not be easy for you because the code given is very long and you need to understand them in order to do the project
sections.teaching: Prof Meng is a nice guy, he is passionate at answering questions. However the lecture slides were so long that it took 70 to 100+ pages for each lecture, but don't worry, they were often duplicate contents (animation), so the real approximate length was 40-50 pages.
sections.grading:
4 assignments, 10% each
1 project, 4 checkpoints, for each of the checkpoint, 5% each
midterm 20%
final 30%

total = 110%
If you get a 90% or above, you will get at least a A-.
If you get a 80% or above, you will get at least a B-.
If you get a 70% or above, you will get at least a C-.
If you get a 60% or above, you will get at least a D.

Important thing:
1. You can have a double-sided A4 cheatsheet for both midterm and final.
2. Even if you perform bad in the midterm, don't give up, there is a policy that if you have a >10% better percentile than your midterm, your midterm will be replaced by the midterm score of (your final percentile - 10%) in your final grade.

My midterm only 59/100 but my final 88/100 and I got A- at last, even though I gave up on checkpoint 4.
sections.workload: The 4 assignments and 4 checkpoints are designed to be done one week after one week i.e. one assignment, and then one checkpoint, and then one assignment. First two checkpoints were easy, but the last two were very difficult.

About the project which is the most diffcult part of this course, this year we are required to change a UDP to TCP (implement congestion control, silding window and loss recovery for packet loss) . Lab 1 is just add a line like helloworld in the code and zip it.

The hard part is that your code relay on the previous lab that you did and he wont release any answer of the lab after the lab. And i can guarantee you that you will not understand any part of the original UDP if you do not have any real world work experience about coding. COMP 2011 last lab looks like easy task compare to this. So in the end you will have no idea what the code is about, where does you need to modify and wtf did you just do. The tutorial mention 0 thing about coding, and just focus on what you need to implement. Add up the mistakes that you made and you will have a complete mess. They only test the whole thing in the final lab ( entire packet received with no loss in a lossy link). but that just account for 1.25% for the whole course.

The workload for the midterm and exam is basically none. SInce there is no pastpaper. Just revivse the hw and remember what you watch in zoom recording is enough ( at least enough for A-)

sections.content: The contents are referenced from CMU. It is a good overview of the whole networking architecture (from Link layer to Application layer) with a few more detailed lectures about the professor's own field of interest(video streaming services networking stuff)
sections.teaching: The teaching is not bad. Prof is willing to help and respond to email regularly and always available. But the lack of resources might be a struggle during midterms and homework, even with the help of the professor.
sections.grading: The grading is rather lenient. I missed almost 80% of my project. I handed in all of my homework with most of my homework being above 80% and one with under 60%. My midterm was slightly above mean and my finals being 20 marks above mean. This landed me a B+. Well, the course grade distribution was also interesting. Most of the grades were depended on the assignments with each assignments counted for 7% of the grade and there was 5 homework.
sections.workload: The workload is quite heavy considering we need to build on the starter code for the project. As a 3 credit course, writing a whole TCP protocol with only a little bit of background in C is incredibly stressful. The TAs that were responsible of the codes wrote the codes in their own convenience without any explanation. Even worse, the TAs did not even help in a bit during tutorials and provided 0 assistance throughout the whole project period. The project was also initiated right after the midterm ended. The project ended at the last week of the semester which almost made it almost impossible to study for the finals beforehand.

sections.content:
The course use the bottom up approach to teach. Starting from the physical layer to the application layer, for the details of the topic, you may refer to different reviews.

At the week of the midterm and last week of teaching, Prof. Meng will use a lecture and the tutorial to review the contents and provide exercise for us to do. In which the exercise are much more difficult than the exam paper.
sections.teaching:
The teaching is excellent, Prof. Meng will use candy to encourage students to answer/ask questions in the lectures.

Since this is the first semester for him, so he overestimated the usefulness of COMP1021. Therefore, the project was a nightmare for most of the students (and many of them gave up).

Prof. Meng will take in charge of this course again in 24-25 Fall and he said he will change the per-request to COMP2011, and will change the content of Project 0. For the new project 0, it will teach students how to use git.

sections.content:
The content are shown in the comment below. The textbook is "Computer Networking: a Top down Approach" which is widely used in computer networking course. And ppt is directly used from the one authors of the textbook made. This course covers the first six chapters. So textbook can provide more detail about the course material.
This course is an introductory course. If you are beginners of computer network, which means you have the following questions in your mind like me before taking this course:
(1) Why does the speed(bandwidth) of wireless network in library is slow in the afternoon when there are increasing students?
(2) I often heard about http, ip, what are they and what is the difference between them?
(3) What do we mean by ip address xx.xx.xx.xx ?
Is ip address dynamic or static?
(4) How do we surf the internet?
(5) What is the difference between host, server, data center?
This course will tell you all the answers.
However, this course does not cover advanced material like: (1) socket programming(only theory, no programming practice)  (2) network security(only talk a few words in the introduction), wireless and mobile network, multimedia networking (in all, none of the last three chapters of the textbook) If you would like to learn more, consider go to COMP course.
sections.teaching: Prof mainly reads the note and sometimes add some explanation. It may be boring sometime since this course is more about lots of man-made protocol and theory. But I think prof is nice and you can discuss with him any questions you don't understand in class and his explanation is detailed and satisfactory. For tutorial, some of the classes are used to review the content we learn in the previous week, while the rest is used for giving explanations and hint in homework (very important).

sections.workload:
This semester only four pieces of written assignment. Each takes around 2-3h. So it is much lighter compared to COMP courses.
This semester prof cuts the socket programming assignment (maybe because it is difficult) and replace that 10% with attendance. But I think socket programming is important in networking(maybe programming is important in networking which is similar to operating system) so I think this assignment can be recovered in the future offerings.

sections.teaching:
This course consists of lecture and tutorial only, both of which don't require attendance.

As for the teaching, it's one of the worst, but what a typical lecturer does in university. You hear the monotone voice from the professor in lectures, and Powerpoint slides being displayed one after another as he reads from the slides.

Like others said, tutorial provides some hints to the questions given in each assignment, but they're not really relevant to the problems you're going to complete. As for the programming assignment, you need a bit of knowledge of Python in order to understand how to make a TCP/UDP server work properly.

The TAs can be a bit more helpful instead of saying "The ability of searching online smartly is crucial for one’s learning. We are all learners in some sense." in the slides. Otherwise, what are the TAs here for? You're only using this as an excuse to shove others away from asking questions.

In the end, all the assignments are a waste of time. You need to search all over the Internet in order to find the solutions for the assignments. I'd have allocated these time to do something meaningful if not for the requirement.
sections.grading:

Midterm and final are both conducted online. You're expected to write your answers, scan them and upload them to Canvas.

It's the annoying type of exam, because the professor isn't really considerate about our situation. According to their rules, we're required to use the smartphones as cameras, and use the very same device to scan the papers. How do you expect us to use the smartphone without leaving the camera on? It's not possible.
sections.workload: As long as you know how to look for solutions in Google and Stack Overflow as the TAs said, the workload isn't that heavy. Still, it's time-consuming.
